label: first copy output (recall 1) in L=9 sequences; delimiter step in L=3 sequences
explanation: Never fires during the original phase. It fires at one sequence-length-dependent position near the start of recall. (a) At the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, input = orig(0)) in long sequences: L=9 holds about 69% of activation mass, where roughly half of L=9 sequences fire; L=8 fires weakly (about 12% of mass, 13% rate). (b) At the <DEL> step itself in L=3 sequences (about 16% of mass, 69% rate); L=4 fires rarely. Within these positions, whether it fires and how strongly depends on the tokens in a graded way, not a crisp set: higher when the first token is 3, d, m, k or t (top L=3 examples look like d ? n). Adding a first-token set raises precision to about 0.79 but costs too much recall. It does not fire at recall_idx >= 2, at medium lengths (L=5-7), or in the original phase. Magnitudes are small (median 0.017, max 0.108).
